adoption.comparison: Recent use: Q1 19.1% → Q2 21.7% → Q3 23.8% (+2.1 percentage points from Q2). Latest: +0.8 points from Q3. Expected use: Q2 24.5% → Q3 27.7% → latest 28.6%.
adoption.limits: Quarter figures are selected reference windows, not averages. The latest window, September 21–October 4, spans two quarters. History uses the October workbook; expectations are not outcomes.
adoption.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Business Trends and Outlook Survey; October 22, 2026 release, October 27 workbook.

employment.comparison: Q2-end June: -4.3% / 0.0%. Q3-end September: -3.7% / +0.2%. The high-exposure annual growth rate rose +0.6 percentage points.
employment.limits: Quarter-end months, each compared with a year earlier; not quarterly job losses. Separate releases may use different samples or revised estimates. Exposure does not establish AI causation. Q4 outcomes are not yet available.
employment.source: ADP Research; June release July 22 and September release October 21, 2026.

census.scope: Two comparable historical readings / Q4 remains open

metrics.label: Young high-exposure employment growth / September vs June

census.comparison: Adoption: 21.7% → 23.8%. Employment annual growth: −4.3% → −3.7%. Percentage points measure the difference between rates; these two indicators describe different populations.
census.limits: Adoption uses quarter reference snapshots from one workbook. Employment uses quarter-end months from separate releases, not quarterly losses or an estimate of AI causation.
census.source: U.S. Census Bureau, October workbook; ADP Research, July 22 and October 21, 2026 releases.
census.comparison_basis: Quarter reference snapshots and quarter-end months

metrics.label: Maximum budget and time per attempt

capability.comparison: Initial publication snapshot: no preserved, comparable earlier-quarter export. Future comparisons must keep the problems, tools, budget and scoring consistent.
capability.limits: Best reported configuration: GPT-6.1 Sol (max); one attempt per conjecture. A specialist mathematics test, not a general intelligence ranking. Few successes make rankings uncertain.
capability.source: Epoch AI, FrontierMath Erdős methods and October 28 data export; CC BY 4.0.

prices.comparison: First saved price baseline; no like-for-like earlier-quarter capture. These are charges for equal billed quantities, not equal-quality results.
prices.limits: One million input plus 250,000 output tokens (pieces of billed text); prompts at most 100,000 tokens. Excludes discounts, tools, retries, taxes and human checking.
prices.source: Anthropic model documentation and OpenAI release notes; rates checked October 28, 2026. Basket charges calculated by AIEVOQ.

energy.scope: All data centres worldwide / IEA 2026 outlook
energy.comparison: Annual estimate and future projection, not two quarterly observations. No comparable earlier-quarter consumption figure is available in this series.
energy.limits: Both include non-AI computing. One terawatt-hour (TWh) is one billion kilowatt-hours. Carry the estimate with its year; compare revisions to the same forecast year separately.
energy.source: International Energy Agency, Key Questions on Energy and AI, 2026 executive summary.

math-catalogue.comparison: The collection was released in October. No comparable earlier-quarter catalogue snapshot is recorded.
math-catalogue.limits: Counts of proposed research, not accepted breakthroughs or independent results. Several manuscripts can belong to one family; checking stages vary.
math-catalogue.source: OpenAI mathematics repository, README inspected October 27, 2026.

haiku.comparison: +56.7 percentage points between model versions. This is a comparison published together in Q4, not a measured Q3-to-Q4 trend.
haiku.limits: Anthropic’s evaluation; no independent rerun or uncertainty estimate in this record. Test success does not establish everyday workplace reliability.

funding.comparison: A new announced commitment. No comparable earlier-quarter total is recorded.
funding.limits: Simons Foundation, Anthropic and OpenAI partnership. The figure includes resources and is not a total already spent or a count of validated results.

learning.scope: High-school mathematics / background study published June 2025

metrics.label: Later unaided exam grades / GPT Base

learning.comparison: Both are relative to the no-AI control group, not quarter-to-quarter changes. Different tests: do not subtract them to produce a “learning loss” score.
learning.limits: One school, nearly 1,000 students. The teaching-oriented GPT Tutor largely avoided the exam penalty. Short-run results do not establish career-long effects.
learning.source: Bastani and colleagues, PNAS, June 25, 2025; abstract and Table 1.

workplace-gains.scope: Customer support / background study published February 2025

metrics.label: Average issues resolved per hour with AI access

workplace-gains.comparison: Effect estimated during a staggered introduction of AI at one firm; not an earlier-quarter series. A new study would not be a trend unless its methods and population matched.
workplace-gains.limits: Gains varied across workers. This is a work-output measure, not a 15% wage gain, headcount reduction or economy-wide productivity estimate.
workplace-gains.source: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond, Generative AI at Work, Quarterly Journal of Economics; published February 4, 2025.

barclays.comparison: A forecast associated with full-year 2026 cost actions, not completed Q4 losses. No comparable prior-quarter AI-only figure is available.
barclays.limits: AI’s separate contribution is unquantified; other organizational and technology changes are included. Subject to consultation.
barclays.source: Barclays Q3 2026 results presentation, slide 10 and footnotes 3–4; October 22.

metrics.label: Consultants in the published Nature study
IT apprentices in the IZA working paper
Share of available task marks / two beyond-training tasks in the IZA study

task-expansion.comparison: Separate experiments, not quarterly trend observations. IZA fieldwork: October 2025–January 2026; journal abstract does not specify the consultants’ test dates.
task-expansion.limits: The task gains are percentage points, not wage gains. Immediate comprehension and later unaided knowledge are different outcomes. The IZA paper is not yet peer reviewed.
task-expansion.source: Wiles and colleagues, Nature Human Behaviour, October 26; Brosch and colleagues, IZA DP18999, October 2026, pages 12–18.

research-automation.scope: Anthropic’s own AI research and development
research-automation.comparison: A Q3 month versus a Q1 month, not whole-quarter averages. The report provides no matched Q4 reading.
research-automation.limits: Company-reported ratings: “leads” still includes human supervision. No measured subset was fully autonomous in the August snapshot. This is not an industry-wide measure.
research-automation.source: Anthropic, Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs; August 2026 snapshot.

agent-teams.scope: Research agents / background report published June 2025

metrics.label: Relative performance gain on one internal evaluation

agent-teams.comparison: Opus 4 leading Sonnet 4 helpers versus Opus 4 alone. A system comparison reported together, not a quarterly improvement rate or a 90.2-point rise.
agent-teams.limits: Anthropic’s own research evaluation. Team coordination and additional computing have costs; this result does not apply to every task or every team.
agent-teams.source: Anthropic, How we built our multi-agent research system, June 13, 2025.

agent-design.scope: Earlier research / 2025 / not an Elephant-Goldfish test
agent-design.comparison: A background study, not a Q4 2026 trend. No comparable earlier-quarter plugin outcome data are available.
agent-design.limits: Study counts, not a failure rate or an improvement score. The 14 failure types were defined from 150 recorded runs; the larger collection used AI-assisted labeling. It did not include Elephant-Goldfish.
agent-design.source: Cemri et al., Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?, arXiv v3, October 26, 2025; checked October 30, 2026.
agent-design.comparison_basis: Earlier research / no quarterly plugin comparison

7.entry: OpenAI. **Model Release Notes.** October 14 and October 26, 2026 entries. Figure: Terra standard input/output rates of $1/$5 per million tokens. Retirement scope is product-specific. https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9624314-model-release-notes

11.entry: OpenAI. **Mathematics repository, README.** Live catalogue inspected October 27: 721 manuscripts, 373 families. Verification stages vary. Those totals are a dated snapshot and differ from widely reported initial-release counts. https://github.com/openai/math

15.entry: Simons Foundation. **Simons Foundation Launches $15M Effort To Help Mathematicians Navigate AI Era.** October 15, 2026. Describes a combined funding-and-resources commitment, not a payment made to this project. https://www.simonsfoundation.org/news/simons-foundation-launches-15m-effort-to-help-mathematicians-navigate-ai-era/

29.entry: Anthropic. **How we built our multi-agent research system.** June 13, 2025. The 90.2% gain is relative, on an internal research evaluation, for Opus 4 leading Sonnet 4 helpers versus Opus 4 alone. Costs and coordination limitations accompany the finding. https://www.anthropic.com/research/multi-agent-research-system

30.entry: Anthropic. **Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs.** Company-reported August 2026 snapshot. Its research-automation index distinguishes supervised leadership from full autonomy; the 26% figure does not establish a self-directed successor-development cycle. https://www.anthropic.com/institute/measuring-pace-of-ai-development

44.entry: Hamsa Bastani and colleagues. **Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics.** PNAS, June 25, 2025. Peer-reviewed field experiment in one Turkish high school, with nearly a thousand students. Unrestricted assistance improved assisted practice but reduced subsequent unaided performance; a teaching-oriented design largely mitigated that loss. Short educational setting, not a career-length study. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122

46.entry: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li and Lindsey Raymond. **Generative AI at Work.** Quarterly Journal of Economics 140(2), 889-942, 2025. Peer-reviewed study of an assistant's staggered introduction among 5,172 support agents. Benefits were strongest among less experienced and lower-performing workers; the authors also report evidence consistent with learning. One workplace, a different task and study design from [44]-[45]; this is a useful counterweight, not a direct replication. https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjae044

74.entry: International Energy Agency. **Key Questions on Energy and AI.** 2026 report, executive summary. Estimates global data-centre electricity use at 485 TWh in 2025 and projects around 950 TWh in 2030. These totals include non-AI data centres. Discusses efficiency, changing tasks and infrastructure constraints. Institutional energy analysis, not a peer-reviewed experiment; projections depend on assumptions and are not promises about realized demand. https://www.iea.org/reports/key-questions-on-energy-and-ai/executive-summary

79.entry: Nela Richardson / ADP Research. **Canaries Dashboard: Employment in AI-exposed occupations shrank in September.** October 21, 2026. U.S. private-employer payroll data: September 2026 against September 2025. The chart reproduces all-age and age-22-25 comparisons; it does not estimate causal AI job losses. https://www.adpresearch.com/research/canaries-dashboard-employment-in-ai-exposed-occupations-shrank-in-september/

82.entry: Barclays. **Q3 2026 Results Presentation**, October 22, slide 10 and footnotes 3-4. Expected workforce reduction from full-year structural cost actions, subject to consultation; management's estimate, not an AI-only attribution. Original presentation saved and read. https://home.barclays/content/dam/home-barclays/documents/investor-relations/ResultAnnouncements/Q32026Results/Q326-Results-Presentation.pdf

84.entry: Emma Wiles, Lisa Krayer, Mohamed Abbadi, Urvi Awasthi, Ryan Kennedy, Pamela Mishkin, Daniel Sack and Francois Candelon. **Generative AI and the temporary upskilling of knowledge workers.** Nature Human Behaviour, published October 26, 2026. Peer-reviewed randomized study. The journal abstract reports 487 consultants. BCG supported the research with employee time and resources; company-affiliated authors participated in the study. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-026-02566-6

85.entry: Hanna Brosch, Christina Langer, Philipp Lergetporer, Sandra Mueller, Harald Pfeifer and Nele Tschoepe. **Task Expansion with Generative AI: Experimental Evidence on Middle-Skilled, Early-Career Workers.** IZA Discussion Paper 18999, October 2026; exact release day not established. Data collected October 2025-January 2026. Pages 12-18 define scoring and report the effects. https://docs.iza.org/dp18999.pdf

86.entry: U.S. Census Bureau. **Business Trends and Outlook Survey, National Estimates**, workbook downloaded October 27, 2026; latest release October 22. Response Estimates, Response Standard Errors, and Collection and Reference Dates sheets. This edition retains 24 waves beginning with the November 17, 2025 collection period. Historical quarter snapshots are reconstructed from this one workbook, using the final reference window wholly within each quarter; they are not quarter averages or a record of what was known on each quarter's last day. https://www.census.gov/hfp/btos/data_downloads

87.entry: ADP Research. **Canaries Dashboard**, June 2026 observation, published July 22, 2026. High/least exposure annual employment growth: all ages -0.2%/+0.6%; ages 22-25 -4.3%/0.0%. https://www.adpresearch.com/research/canaries-dashboard-2026-june

90.entry: Epoch AI. **FrontierMath Erdős**, benchmark description and methodology; consulted October 28, 2026. The suite contains 68 conjectures from 65 distinct numbered Erdős problems, curated with Thomas Bloom, and uses formally checked proofs. One attempt per conjecture, $300 and 72 hours per attempt. Different test budgets and expanded experiments are excluded from the standard comparison. https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/frontiermath-erdos

91.entry: Epoch AI. **Capabilities & benchmarking: Use this data.** Export downloaded October 28, 2026; FrontierMath Erdős table and associated model metadata. Thirteen evaluated configurations. Some source scores are rounded; do not infer exact solved-item counts from every displayed percentage. The leading row is exactly 3/68. These are Epoch's own evaluations, licensed CC BY 4.0; chart adaptation by AIEVOQ. The export's run timestamps and model release dates do not establish when every result became public. https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/use-this-data
